clue.text: Henry's imprisoned in half of castle in Conway — it's brutal

indicators.note: in places the castle-and-Henry piece inside the pianist's first name

parts.note: Russ Conway was a popular British pianist of the late 1950s and early 1960s

indicators.note: imprisoned in means Henry is locked up inside the piece from the castle
half of takes the back three of the six letters of castle

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for henry, the unit of inductance; the 's is 'is'

explanation.surface: A Welsh castle town where an English king is held prisoner in brutal fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: Conway suggests the Welsh castle town (Conwy), but it is the pianist Russ Conway; 'half of', 'imprisoned in' and 'in' do the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Being without pity or mercy is what makes conduct savage and brutal.

clue.text: Courier, without right vehicle tax, made anxious

indicators.note: without tells us the letter for right is dropped from the messenger

parts.note: a runner is a messenger or courier
VED is Vehicle Excise Duty, the British road tax on cars

explanation.surface: A delivery rider loses their nerve over the car tax bill.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' removes R from RUNNER to leave UNNER. VED (Vehicle Excise Duty) is Britain's annual road tax on vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who has lost their nerve has been rattled and made anxious.

clue.text: Author's regular publication that's seen in nursery?

parts.note: Thomas Hardy, English novelist and poet
an annual is a book or magazine published once a year

explanation.surface: A novelist has a yearly book that children read in the nursery.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's stands for 'has'. 'Nursery' suggests children's books, but it is a plant nursery, where such hardy flowering plants are sold.
explanation.definitionFit: A plant that completes its life cycle in a year and can withstand frost is the kind of stock a garden centre or nursery raises.

clue.text: Drunken sprees rising because of premium drink

indicators.note: drunken signals that the letters of sprees are reeling about and rearranged
rising in a down clue means the word for because is read upwards, i.e. backwards

parts.note: 'cos is the colloquial short form of because
a premium is a fee or payment, as on an insurance policy

explanation.surface: Boozy binges are getting more frequent because of the cost of drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rising' in a down clue turns the slangy 'cos upwards; 'Drunken' scrambles the sprees.
explanation.definitionFit: A strong coffee made by forcing steam through ground beans is a drink.

clue.text: Clothing matters to become mater's when this is shed?

definitions.meaning: a sleeveless vest is an item of clothing

definitions.text: matters to become mater's when this is shed?
definitions.meaning: removing one T from the word matters leaves mater's, so the thing shed is a lone T

explanation.surface: A garment that turns things that count into a mother's possessions when taken off.
explanation.walkthrough: The second definition reads the answer as SINGLE T: drop one T from MATTERS and it becomes MATER'S (mater is old schoolboy Latin for mother).
explanation.definitionFit: A vest or sleeveless top is a garment, and read as two words it describes one lone letter T.

clue.text: Love to join some of sandwich courses here

indicators.note: to join here means the letter for love is fitted into the layer

parts.note: a ply is a layer, and a layer is part of a sandwich
O is love, a nil score in tennis

explanation.surface: A romantic urge to take part in some sandwich-course study.
explanation.walkthrough: POLY is short for polytechnic, a British college of higher education known for 'sandwich courses' that alternate study with work placements.
explanation.definitionFit: A polytechnic was a college offering degree courses, so courses are held there.

clue.text: One convincing bloodstained Australia players to retreat …

indicators.note: to retreat means the whole string of pieces goes backwards

parts.note: bloodstained things are red
rep, a repertory company, is a group of players

explanation.surface: A bloodied Australian team being pushed back by a forceful opponent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to retreat' turns the whole run RED + AUS + REP backwards, giving PERSUADER.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who talks another round is a persuader, one who convinces.

clue.text: … made a touchdown, England shortly converting it. Class!

parts.note: an aircraft that has made a touchdown has landed

indicators.note: converting means the abbreviation for England is changed into a new order

parts.note: ENG is the short form of England
it refers back to the touchdown, which in rugby is a try

explanation.surface: England score a rugby try and convert it: what class!
explanation.walkthrough: The rugby picture is the trick: 'it' stands for the touchdown, a TRY, and 'converting' shuffles ENG into GEN.
explanation.definitionFit: The landed gentry are a social class of landowners below the nobility.

clue.text: Government official creates building in Irish city fronted by peacekeepers

indicators.note: fronted by means the peacekeepers' letters stand at the front

parts.note: UN, the United Nations, sends peacekeeping forces

indicators.note: in puts the rearranged letters inside the Irish city

parts.note: Derry is a city in Northern Ireland

indicators.note: building suggests the letters of creates are being constructed into something new

explanation.surface: An official puts up a new building in Derry with United Nations backing.
explanation.walkthrough: Derry (Londonderry) is in Northern Ireland; 'building' is the anagram signal, not the noun, and 'fronted by' puts the peacekeepers first.
explanation.definitionFit: A junior minister or senior civil servant ranking below a secretary is a government official.

clue.text: Open no. 4 on menu (prawn crackers)

indicators.note: no. 4 on picks the fourth letter of the word menu
crackers, meaning crazy, signals that the letters of prawn are scrambled

explanation.surface: A diner orders number four on the Chinese menu, prawn crackers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crackers' looks like part of the takeaway order but is the anagram signal; 'no. 4 on' picks the fourth letter of the menu.
explanation.definitionFit: To unwrap a parcel is to open it.

clue.text: Type of shirt perhaps something reversible worn by Northern Ireland

indicators.note: worn by places the two abbreviations together with the palindrome, here set inside it

parts.note: noon reads the same backwards, so it is something reversible

explanation.surface: A reversible shirt worn by the Northern Ireland football team.
explanation.walkthrough: Northern Ireland is split into two abbreviations, N and IR, which sit inside the palindrome NOON.
explanation.definitionFit: A shirt that needs no pressing after washing is described this way, so it names a kind of shirt.

clue.text: River comes back in spring, bringing nearly every marine creature

indicators.note: comes back in means the letter for river shifts back towards the front within the spring

parts.note: a geyser is a hot spring

indicators.note: nearly means the word for every loses its final letter

parts.note: all means every

explanation.surface: When a river flows back into the spring it brings nearly every sea creature with it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'comes back in' moves the R in GEYSER towards the front, giving GREYSE; 'nearly' trims ALL to AL.
explanation.definitionFit: This seal species of the North Atlantic is an animal of the sea.

clue.text: Breakfast food you cooked audibly oozed out

indicators.note: audibly says the phrase is to be spoken and heard as one word

parts.note: the breakfast food is eggs, and you cooked them is 'you did' them

explanation.surface: A runny breakfast that you cooked, oozing across the plate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eggs you did' run together in speech sounds like EXUDED.
explanation.definitionFit: Exuding is seeping or oozing out slowly, so the past tense matches 'oozed out'.

clue.text: Stunned, seeing double, Ed is sent to doctor

indicators.note: to doctor means to tamper with, so the letters are rearranged
seeing double tells us the words Ed is are taken twice over

explanation.surface: Dazed and seeing double, Ed is packed off to the doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seeing double' doubles ED IS to EDISEDIS; with SENT that makes twelve letters, which 'to doctor' rearranges.
explanation.definitionFit: Desensitised means made numb or insensitive, as one is when stunned.

clue.text: Complex comedy film character seen in debut for Ang Lee, animating

indicators.note: seen in means the film character appears inside the other letters
animating, bringing to life, signals the letters being stirred into a new order
debut for takes the first letter of the director's first name

parts.note: Borat is the comic character of Sacha Baron Cohen's 2006 film

explanation.surface: A comic film character appears in Ang Lee's first animated film.
explanation.walkthrough: Ang Lee is a film director, which helps the surface; 'animating' is the anagram signal, and 'seen in' places the Sacha Baron Cohen character inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Something elaborate is intricate and detailed, that is, complex.

clue.text: Biscuit female left, before a meal, next to salt

parts.note: a.p. stands for ante prandium, Latin for before a meal, used on prescriptions
a salt is a sailor, as is a jack (jack tar)

explanation.surface: A woman leaves before dinner to sit next to a sailor with her biscuit.
explanation.walkthrough: AP is the prescription abbreviation for 'ante prandium', before meals. In Britain a flapjack is an oat-and-syrup bar.
explanation.definitionFit: A British flapjack is a chewy oat bar, classed with biscuits and traybakes.

clue.text: Parallel bars centrally caught, leading to twitching by a group of people

indicators.note: leading to means these pieces come before the ones that follow
centrally picks the middle letters of the word bars

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a tic is an involuntary twitching
a circle is a group of people with shared interests

explanation.surface: A gymnast on the parallel bars is caught twitching in front of a group of spectators.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Parallel bars' reads as gymnastics, but 'Parallel' is the definition alone: a line of latitude.
explanation.definitionFit: This line of latitude at about 66 degrees north is one of the parallels on a globe.

clue.text: Rock star, like a swine, degrading Prince work

indicators.note: degrading, read as moving down a grade, sends the letter for prince lower in this down entry

parts.note: piggy means pig-like, like a swine
op, short for opus, is a musical work

explanation.surface: A piggish rock star who demeaned the singer Prince's work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'degrading' moves the P (prince) of PIGGY down the entry: PIGGY + OP becomes IGGYPOP.
explanation.definitionFit: Iggy Pop is the American punk singer of the Stooges, a rock star.

clue.text: See 7
Free love outwardly noble

indicators.note: outwardly takes just the outside letters of love

parts.note: a toff is a posh or upper-class person, a noble

explanation.surface: Love that is free, outwardly noble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outwardly' keeps the first and last letters of LOVE, giving LE; TOFF is British slang for a posh person.
explanation.definitionFit: To excuse someone from punishment is to set them free.

clue.text: Animal to consume enriching fruit

indicators.note: enriching means the consuming word goes inside the fruit, adding to it

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
to eat is to consume

explanation.surface: An animal eats some fruit to enrich its diet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to consume' looks like the definition's verb, but 'Animal' alone defines; 'enriching' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas, chimps and orangutans are large primates, animals of this family.

clue.text: More than one X on side of Valentine present perhaps

parts.note: X is the Roman numeral ten, so more than one X is tens

indicators.note: side of takes an edge letter, here the last of Valentine

explanation.surface: Kisses written beside a Valentine card, perhaps with a present.
explanation.walkthrough: X looks like a kiss on a Valentine, but it is the Roman ten. 'present' is not a gift but a grammatical tense.
explanation.definitionFit: The present is one grammatical tense, alongside past and future, so it is an example.

clue.text: Net attracts French couple, mostly to buy superior goods

indicators.note: attracts means the net draws in the other piece, which ends up inside

parts.note: to net is to trap

indicators.note: mostly means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: deux is French for two, a couple

explanation.surface: A net lures a French couple into buying better-quality goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Net' is a verb here, to catch; 'mostly' trims the French word for two before 'attracts' puts it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To exchange something for a more expensive version is to purchase better-quality items.

clue.text: See 3 Down
Mystery trip includes bringing back Mediterranean port

indicators.note: bringing back signals that the letters are read from right to left
includes signals that the letters lie within the words mystery trip

explanation.surface: A mystery tour that brings travellers back from a Mediterranean port.
explanation.walkthrough: Read backwards, 'mysterY TRip' gives the port.
explanation.definitionFit: Tyre is an ancient Phoenician city on the Lebanese coast of the Mediterranean.

clue.text: Daughter enters passkey, working here in bank?

indicators.note: enters means the letter for daughter goes inside the rearranged word
working here signals that the letters of passkey are put to work in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A daughter types in a passkey while working at the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'working' rearranges PASSKEY, and D goes inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Counters where money is paid in or out are found in a bank, with the question mark marking a definition by example.
